term: structural dependency graph, source, terminal and fixed-point semantics
definition: Graph.edge y x points from upstream y to dependent x. A source has no incoming upstream edge; a terminal has no outgoing downstream edge. NoCycles forbids every nonempty finite return path. Controls combines no cycles, no infinite descending Nat-indexed series, and a finite path from each node to some relative source. Map preserves edges and pulls accessibility back. transmission sends S to intrinsic nodes together with nodes having an upstream member in S; its least fixed point is exactly FinitelyGroundedPower, whereas its greatest fixed point can admit source-free activity.
note: Mathematical graph vocabulary only. Graph sources need not be temporally first, unique, globally independent, existent in an interpreted world, or divine. FinitelyGroundedPower is reused for its parameterized inductive structure; this is not an identification of actual power with finite paths. Knaster–Tarski uses Mathlib.
